questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: All of the aspects listed above were important to me! The opportunity to study on a foreign university with talented professors and students have definitely been an experience both academic and cultural. Living abroad has been amazing – and my destination was a dream coming true.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy, though I spent a lot of time trying to figure the foreign system out, but had good help from the local Erasmus coordinator.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Mails and personal contact with local institute Erasmus coordinator and orientation days and local students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was a bit tough, but I used my network and found a good solution!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
I lived with 3 other exchange students which was super nice in terms of all of us being in more or less the same situation. We lived in connection to the Danish church in Berlin, which was a good experience since I became part of a community where I could also gather advice from other 'expats'.
I though also think living with local roomies might also be great to dig deeper into the local culture.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Registration for courses on my institute could be done in an online portal, but for all other courses I had to contact the respective professor and get their permission to follow the course.
It's very different how many ECTS the different types of courses are worth from institute to institute so that was very difficult to get a hold on – I had to ask each professor who was sometimes also not sure. Also I was (and still is) unsure how the exams function; you can choose to write an essay (Hausarbeit) in the end of a seminar to obtain extra credits, but I found it difficult to find out if you needed to or not, because in some seminars it was mandatory, but in others you just needed active participation to get the credits.
Furthermore local students have to complete modules (often 2 seminars) with one exam at the end, but it was not clear whether or not Erasmus students had to. I was told in the orientation days that this rule did not apply to Erasmus students in any institute, but in the last week of the semester I was told that I could not be credited for the one course I had followed on the institute of philosophy, because it was not in a module. I talked back and forth with my institute coordinator, my professor and the secretary on the institute of philosophy and ended up getting permission to get the ECTS if I prolonged an upcoming essay, so it would be 6 pages instead of 3. This was three days before the essay was due and in the last week of the semester, so I was also rather hung up in the other courses, but my professor accepted that I handed in the essay a few days later. It was though very stressful – and from talking to other (local) students I've now been made aware that the module rule does not apply to Erasmus students, just as I was initially told. Everything ended up fine, but I just didn't find it a very nice process.
Nevertheless I found that I learned a lot from my confusion in the process – I think part of the experience abroad is also this trying to get your head around foreign rules and systems and handling this frustration and uncertainty :))

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
It took me a while to get to understand the system and I got a lot of help from other exchange student, local students and my Erasmus coordinator.
Though I received good help, I often felt very stupid with all my questions and that the coordinator and professors were tired of exchange students being confused about the course registration.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I think the courses I ended up following were super good, but it took a long time to get there ;))

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress too much about course registration. Everyone is interested in you completing the courses and having a good experience, though it sometimes seem like everyone is trying to make it more difficult. You'll get there!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very nice courses and professors, though it is frustrating that the course offering changes so much from semester to semester.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Very much the same level as in Copenhagen. High quality! :-)

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
There was a bigger formality in the style of teaching and a bigger "status gap" between the students and the professors (eg. by the use of formal address or last name) – which I found overwhelming but also good for the environment. It was though something that both students and professors addressed from time to other as a problem.
Furthermore I found that the students also were more "loyal" to what was said by the professor and didn't necessarily ask critical questions, but it was difficult from course to course.
But overall I was very pleased with the teaching!

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer: The courses offered changes so much from semester to semester, so I cannot recommend any particular courses!

questions.answer: Grocery-shopping was cheaper than back home! Also food and coffee on campus.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There were student sports and orchestras, which I didn't take part in. Also a few Erasmus student social opportunities.
Mostly I took part in the campus student cafés which I enjoyed. But I found it a bit overwhelming to seek information about non-academic opportunities on campus in the beginning of the semester because I used all my energy studying and trying to understand the course systems, and then, when I was more settled, I found it was a bit too late to engage later on. So I ended up mostly using the other offers of the city. Maybe it would make sense to inform about eg. open spots at the sport opportunities throughout the semester where the Erasmus students maybe have more energy to engage?

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Use the cafes on campus, and talk to the local students there! They know what's nice to do and will probably offer you to join them

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Enjoy the beautiful city and all it offers! I didn't do any weekend trips as I just felt like exploring the city

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don't be too afraid to engage!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The way German people often correct you (a bit offensive) in the street eg. if you are in their way, don't have lights on your bike or something else they find annoying about you...

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I though enjoyed the diversity of the city and the university, eg. how differently people dressed.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't stress too much about the course registration! Ask other exchange students and use all the ressources you can think of.
Don't be afraid of approaching strangers, eg. other students on university. Danes are so reserved, and it doesn't make any new friendships!
Don't spend too much time studying – it's also important to socialise, engage with local culture and experience a lot of things!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Enjoy it as much as you can!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The cultural experience and knowing that I am academically and personally capable of living and studying abroad :-)

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The German bureaucratic system ...

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
